Complicated relationships with fellow revolutionaries caused him to be expelled from the International Workingmen's Association.

Once you see Sergei Nechaev as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. While locked up in a ravelin of the fortress, Nechaev managed to win over his guards with the strength of his convictions and by the late 1870s was using them to pass on correspondence with revolutionaries on the outside. In December 1880, Nechaev established contact with the executive committee of the People's Will (Narodnaya Volya) and proposed a plan for his own escape.
